independent_solution: Test each quantity: does specifying it completely require a direction? If yes it is a vector (magnitude + direction, triangle law); if no it is a scalar.
Volume, mass, density and number of moles are fully given by a number and unit; speed is the magnitude of velocity and angular frequency is 2*pi/T, both without direction -> scalars.
Acceleration, velocity, displacement and angular velocity (axis direction) need a direction -> vectors.
questions.independent_answer: Scalars: volume, mass, speed, density, number of moles, angular frequency. Vectors: acceleration, velocity, displacement, angular velocity.
questions.official_answer: Volume, mass, speed, density, number of moles, angular frequency are scalars; the rest (acceleration, velocity, displacement, angular velocity) are vectors.

independent_solution: All three girls start at P and end at Q, so they share one displacement vector PQ, independent of route.
Q is diametrically opposite P, so |PQ| = diameter = 2 x 200 m = 400 m for each girl.
Displacement magnitude equals path length only for a route that never changes direction; in Fig. 3.19 (read on the pinned page) girl B skates straight along the diameter, so only for B.
questions.independent_answer: 400 m for each girl; equal to the path length only for girl B.

independent_solution: Average speed = path length / time = 23 km / 0.4667 h = 49.3 km/h.
Average velocity magnitude = displacement / time = 10 km / 0.4667 h = 21.4 km/h. Not equal: the path is not straight, so path length > displacement.
questions.independent_answer: (a) 49.3 km/h; (b) 21.4 km/h; not equal (they coincide only for a straight path).
questions.official_answer: (a) 49.3 km/h; (b) 21.4 km/h. No, the average speed equals average velocity magnitude only for a straight path.
